lessons.title: Bridge: who am I? Personal details, family and 'I have'
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I introduce myself fully and accurately for a GCSE speaking or writing task?
objectives: To understand how to give developed personal details using عِنْدِي / لَدَيَّ, numbers and agreement
successCriteria: All: give name, age, home and family in full sentences
Most: use عِنْدِي and لَدَيَّ with correct number agreement
Some: develop each answer with a reason, opinion or second time frame
lessons.crossCurricular: English: developing spoken answers (point, detail, opinion)
lessons.smsc: Social: speaking about family with respect and privacy

hook.text: An examiner asks: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِكَ (Tell me about yourself). What makes a Grade 4 answer different from a Grade 8 answer?
hook.a: Range (connectives, tenses, opinions) and accuracy, not just length.

islamicLink.text: Allah made us peoples and tribes so that we may know one another (al-Hujurat 49:13). Introducing ourselves well is the first step in that.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I live in London': A) أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ B) أَنَا لَنْدَنُ

starter.a: For example: عُمْرِي خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً

teach.heading: Personal details

head: Question
Answer
rows: عُمْرِي أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ / خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً
أَسْكُنُ فِي ... فِي شَمَالِ / جَنُوبِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Teach in Arabic where possible (about 70% this year). Pupils may describe a real or made-up family.

teach.heading: Two ways to say 'I have'
teach.note: Both take the owned thing in the nominative. Negative: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي / لَيْسَ لَدَيَّ.

teach.heading: Numbers and family
bullets: 1, 2: noun alone or dual: أَخٌ، أَخَوَانِ
3 to 10: plural, number flips gender: ثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَةٍ، ثَلَاثُ أَخَوَاتٍ
11+: singular accusative: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ ابْنَ عَمٍّ
teach.note: Group A: name the rule in Arabic: العَدَدُ يُخَالِفُ المَعْدُودَ (3 to 10 take the opposite gender).

teach.heading: Model: a developed answer

model.problem: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ أُسْرَتِكَ.
steps: Point: فِي أُسْرَتِي خَمْسَةُ أَشْخَاصٍ.
Detail: لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
Opinion and reason: أَنَا قَرِيبٌ مِنْ أَخِي الكَبِيرِ لِأَنَّهُ يُسَاعِدُنِي.
Second time frame: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ مَعًا.
model.answer: Four linked sentences with range

teach.note: This is the shape for the 1AA0 conversation and for 4AA1 writing.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: أُخْت is feminine, so 3 takes the masculine form ثَلَاثُ, with a plural noun.

practice.q: Answer in two developed sentences: أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟
practice.a: For example: أَسْكُنُ فِي مَدِينَةِ لِيسْتَر فِي وَسَطِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا. أُحِبُّ مَدِينَتِي لِأَنَّهَا هَادِئَةٌ وَفِيهَا مَسَاجِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ.
practice.model:
Point: أَسْكُنُ فِي ...
Detail: where it is (فِي وَسَطِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا).
Opinion + reason: أُحِبُّ مَدِينَتِي لِأَنَّهَا ...

practice.q: Translate: I have two brothers but I do not have a sister.
practice.a: لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ لَدَيَّ أُخْتٌ.

practice.q: Say: there are four people in my family.

independent.q: Core: Write 80 words (portal response box) answering: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِكَ وَعَنْ أُسْرَتِكَ. Use عِنْدِي or لَدَيَّ, a number 3 to 10, an opinion and a reason.
independent.a: Marked for: personal details; family with correct number agreement; opinion with لِأَنَّ; connectives; accuracy.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first three sentences live, saying why each number form is chosen.

independent.q: Extend (Group B, 1AA0 conversation): answer aloud for one minute in a breakout room; partner notes connectives used.
independent.a: One-minute developed answer with at least three connectives

independent.q: Stretch (Group A, 4AA1 grammar): give the i'rab of أَخَوَانِ in لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ.
independent.a: مُبْتَدَأٌ مُؤَخَّرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ وَعَلَامَةُ رَفْعِهِ الأَلِفُ لِأَنَّهُ مُثَنًّى (delayed subject, nominative, marked by alif because it is dual)

exit.q: 'I have' (formal) is: A) لَدَيَّ B) لِي C) أَنَا
Big question: what makes an introduction score highly?
exit.a: Developed answers with opinions, reasons, connectives, more than one time frame and accurate agreement.

lessons.homework: Learn your 80-word answer for the conversation (Group B) or redraft it to 120 words with one more time frame (Group A).
lessons.send: SEND: answer frame with sentence starters. EAL: key phrase card. Stretch: add the past habit كُنْتُ + present verb.

lessons.title: Bridge: describing people: agreement, the dual and qualifiers
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I make a description of a person precise and accurate?
objectives: To understand how adjectives agree in gender and number, including the dual, and how qualifiers make descriptions precise
successCriteria: All: describe appearance and character with agreeing adjectives
Most: use the dual correctly: لَهُ عَيْنَانِ بُنِّيَّتَانِ
Some: use qualifiers and a comparison in a paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: English: precise vocabulary and modifiers (very, quite, rather)
lessons.smsc: Moral: good character (akhlaq) matters more than appearance

hook.text: Describe your best friend in three words. Did you choose looks or character? Which tells us more?
hook.a: Character tells us more about who someone is.

islamicLink.text: Allah praised the Prophet ﷺ: 'And indeed you are of a great moral character' (al-Qalam 68:4). In Islam, character is the best description of a person.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I have two brothers': A) لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ B) لَدَيَّ اِثْنَانِ أَخٌ

teach.heading: Appearance and character
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Describe in words only; no pictures of people.

teach.heading: The dual
bullets: عَيْن → عَيْنَانِ (two eyes)
لَهَا عَيْنَانِ خَضْرَاوَانِ
لَهُ أُخْتَانِ لَطِيفَتَانِ
teach.note: Adjectives in the dual agree too: ـَانِ for both noun and adjective. Colours: خَضْرَاء → خَضْرَاوَانِ.

teach.heading: Qualifiers

head: Qualifier
Example
rows: هِيَ خَجُولَةٌ قَلِيلًا: a little shy
أَخِي طَوِيلٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا: fairly tall

teach.note: Qualifiers come after the adjective.

teach.heading: Model: a paragraph

model.problem: صِفْ صَدِيقًا لَكَ (describe a friend).
steps: صَدِيقِي عُمَرُ طَوِيلٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا وَلَهُ شَعْرٌ أَسْوَدُ قَصِيرٌ.
هُوَ مَرِحٌ جِدًّا وَكَرِيمٌ.
هُوَ أَطْوَلُ مِنِّي لٰكِنَّهُ أَصْغَرُ مِنِّي.
أُحِبُّهُ لِأَنَّهُ يُسَاعِدُ الآخَرِينَ دَائِمًا.
model.answer: Appearance, character, comparison, opinion

teach.note: Mark each feature: qualifier, comparison, reason.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Dual noun, dual adjective: أُخْتَانِ لَطِيفَتَانِ.

practice.q: Describe a cheerful, fairly tall female cousin.
practice.a: بِنْتُ عَمِّي مَرِحَةٌ وَطَوِيلَةٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا.
practice.model:
Noun: بِنْتُ عَمِّي (feminine).
Adjectives with ة: مَرِحَةٌ، طَوِيلَةٌ.
Qualifier after: إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا.

practice.q: Make dual: لَهُ عَيْنٌ زَرْقَاءُ.
What does خَجُول mean?

independent.q: Core: Write 70 to 90 words (portal response box): صِفْ شَخْصًا تُعْجَبُ بِهِ (describe someone you admire), with appearance, character, a qualifier, a comparison and a reason.
independent.a: Marked for agreement (gender, dual), qualifiers, comparison with أَفْعَل مِنْ, opinion with reason.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first two sentences about an imaginary teacher.

independent.q: Extend (Group B): prepare a 30-second spoken description for the picture-based task style: يَبْدُو ... (he seems ...).
independent.a: For example: يَبْدُو سَعِيدًا وَمَرِحًا.

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of طَوِيلٌ in صَدِيقِي طَوِيلٌ.
independent.a: خَبَرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ وَعَلَامَةُ رَفْعِهِ الضَّمَّةُ (predicate, nominative, marked by dammah)

exit.q: What does إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا mean? A) fairly B) very C) never
Big question: what makes a description precise?
exit.a: Agreeing adjectives (including dual), qualifiers and comparisons.

lessons.homework: Write a description of two people (dual) you know, e.g. two cousins, with qualifiers.
lessons.send: SEND: adjective bank with m / f / dual forms. EAL: English beside each. Stretch: the plural of adjectives for people: طِوَالٌ، كِرَامٌ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Identity and culture - Who am I?
lessons.title: Friends and relationships
objectives: Talk about friends and why they matter
Use verbs of relationships in the present tense
Give opinions with reasons about friendship
starter: Describe a person in two sentences.
Translate: 'My father is tall and kind'.
Say how many people are in your family.

teach.heading: My best friend
bullets: صَدِيقِي الْمُفَضَّلُ اسْمُهُ عُمَرُ - my favourite friend is called Umar
نَلْتَقِي كُلَّ يَوْمٍ - naltaqī kulla yawmin - we meet every day
أَقْضِي وَقْتًا مَعَهُ - I spend time with him
هُوَ مُخْلِصٌ وَصَادِقٌ - he is loyal and honest
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Introduce the word 'favourite' as الْمُفَضَّلُ. Pupils describe their best friend using vocabulary from Lesson 2. Online learning means friends may be in different places; invite pupils to describe friends in different cities. Respect privacy: no real names if they prefer.

teach.heading: What makes a good friend?
bullets: أَثِقُ بِهِ - I trust him
نَتَسَاعَدُ - we help each other
هُوَ يَسْمَعُنِي - he listens to me
لَا يَكْذِبُ - he does not lie
teach.note: Link to the Islamic ethic of brotherhood and sisterhood. Qur'an 49:10: the believers are but brothers, so make peace between them. Practise using the verbs in sentences. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Disagreements
bullets: أَحْيَانًا نَتَشَاجَرُ - sometimes we argue
ثُمَّ نَتَصَالَحُ - thumma natasālaḥu - then we make up
أَعْتَذِرُ - aʿtadhiru - I apologise
أُسَامِحُهُ - usāmiḥuhu - I forgive him
teach.note: Teach the vocabulary for conflict resolution and use it in sentences. Ask: why is forgiveness important? The Prophet (peace be upon him) said it is not lawful for a Muslim to avoid his brother for more than three nights, and the better of the two is the one who greets first (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Giving opinions on friendship
bullets: فِي رَأْيِي الصَّدَاقَةُ مُهِمَّةٌ - fī ra'yī aṣ-ṣadāqatu muhimma
لِأَنَّ الصَّدِيقَ يُسَاعِدُنِي - because a friend helps me
الْأَصْدِقَاءُ الصَّالِحُونَ مُهِمُّونَ - good friends are important
teach.note: Combine opinion + reason. Use plural agreement: الْأَصْدِقَاءُ الصَّالِحُونَ (sound masculine plural adjective). Model extended answers. Pupils practise a mini-conversation about friendship.

teach.heading: Speaking practice
bullets: هَلْ لَدَيْكَ أَصْدِقَاءُ كَثِيرُونَ؟ - do you have many friends?
مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِكَ؟ - what do you do with your friends?
كَيْفَ هُوَ الصَّدِيقُ الْجَيِّدُ؟ - what is a good friend like?
teach.note: Pupils practise a three-question conversation in pairs. Remind them to give full answers and add detail. Collect examples of good answers. Assess pronunciation and fluency informally.

practice: Say two qualities of a good friend.
Translate: 'We help each other and we trust each other'.
Say: 'Sometimes we argue but then we make up'.
Ask a partner: 'What do you do with your friends?'
independent: Write a 70-word text about your best friend and why you like them.
Role-play a conversation about friendship with a partner.
Record a one-minute speaking answer on 'A good friend'.
exit: Write one sentence about a good friend with a reason.
Say 'I apologise' and 'I forgive him' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word paragraph on 'Friendship is important', with two reasons and one example.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence builders on friendship. EAL: bilingual relationship vocabulary. Stretch: give a short opinion on online friendships using عَبْرَ الْإِنْتَرْنِتِ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Identity and culture - Who am I?
lessons.title: Writing about myself, my family and friends
objectives: Plan and write a structured paragraph
Use a range of structures and linking words
Edit your own work for accuracy
starter: Say one sentence about a friend with a reason.
Describe your sister's appearance in Arabic.
Say 'I trust him' and 'we help each other' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Plan the paragraph
bullets: Introduction: name, age, home
Body: family and friends
Conclusion: opinion
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain that a strong piece of writing in the exam is organised. Use a planning grid: who, what, why. Pupils plan on a mini-whiteboard. Show how to use ideas from Lessons 1–3.

teach.heading: Model paragraph
bullets: اسْمِي عَائِشَةُ وَعُمْرِي أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً - I am 14
أَسْكُنُ فِي بِرْمِنْغْهَامَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي
لِي أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ - I have two brothers and one sister
أُخْتِي صَدِيقَتِي لِأَنَّهَا صَادِقَةٌ
teach.note: Read aloud and gloss. Identify the structures: age, home, family, reason. Ask: what would improve the paragraph? Possible answers: more detail, opinion, connectives. Note: ʿumrī ... sanatan with 14 in the feminine form (أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ).

teach.heading: Linking words
bullets: أَوَّلًا - firstly
بِالْإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذَلِكَ - in addition
لِذَلِكَ - therefore
وَأَخِيرًا - and finally
teach.note: Teach connectives that give the writing a formal tone. Pupils replace وَ with a better connective in the model. Encourage variety. Avoid overuse of one structure. Link to ihsan: strive for excellence.

teach.heading: Editing checklist
bullets: Verb matches subject
Adjective matches noun
Numbers and ة checked
Vowels where needed
teach.note: Teach a four-step checklist. Pupils correct a flawed paragraph containing five errors: غُرْفَةٌ كَبِيرٌ, عُمْرِي خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً, هِيَ يَذْهَبُ, الصَّدِيقَةُ مُخْلِصٌ, أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنٍ. Ask which errors are the most serious.

teach.heading: Exam writing tips
bullets: Answer every bullet point
Aim for the word count
Use a variety of tenses
teach.note: Practise a writing question: 'Describe yourself, your family and your friends.' Plan in four bullets and write 90 words. Remind about timing: 5 minutes planning, 20 minutes writing, 5 minutes checking.

practice: Correct: عُمْرِي خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً.
Join the sentences with لِأَنَّ: أُحِبُّ أُخْتِي / هِيَ لَطِيفَةٌ.
Add a connective: أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ ___ أُحِبُّ الْمَدِينَةَ.
Translate: 'In addition, my friend is loyal'.
independent: Write a 90-word paragraph on 'Myself, my family and my friends'.
Swap with a partner and use the checklist.
Rewrite your paragraph with corrections.
exit: Write one sentence with 'therefore'.
List two items from the editing checklist.
lessons.homework: Redraft your paragraph and prepare to speak it aloud without notes.
lessons.send: SEND: paragraph skeleton and word bank. EAL: bilingual connective list. Stretch: add a comparison between two family members.

lessons.title: Bridge: daily life in the present tense
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I describe daily life for me and for others in the present tense?
objectives: To understand how the present tense changes for each person and how to describe routines with frequency words
successCriteria: All: describe my routine with five present-tense verbs
Most: conjugate a verb for I, you, he, she, we and they
Some: compare my routine with someone else's using frequency words
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: healthy routines, sleep and screen time
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: a Muslim day organised around the five prayers

hook.text: How is a Muslim teenager's day shaped differently from that of someone who does not pray? Think of the times.
hook.a: Fajr before school, Dhuhr and Asr in the day, Maghrib and Isha in the evening shape the routine.

islamicLink.text: Allah says prayer is prescribed at fixed times (an-Nisa' 4:103). The five prayers give a Muslim's day its shape.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Very' is: A) جِدًّا B) قَلِيلًا

teach.heading: One verb, all persons
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Prefixes أَ، تَ، يَ، نَ; suffixes ـِينَ and ـُونَ. Group A: the term حُرُوفُ المُضَارَعَةِ (أَنَيْتُ).

teach.heading: My routine
bullets: أَسْتَيْقِظُ قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ وَأُصَلِّي
أَتَنَاوَلُ الفَطُورَ ثُمَّ أَبْدَأُ دُرُوسِي عَبْرَ الإِنْتَرْنِتِ
فِي المَسَاءِ أُرَاجِعُ القُرْآنَ وَأَنَامُ مُبَكِّرًا
teach.note: Add time phrases: فِي الصَّبَاحِ، بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ، فِي المَسَاءِ.

teach.heading: How often?
teach.note: أَبَدًا needs a negative before the verb.

teach.heading: Model: comparing routines

model.problem: Compare my routine and my brother's.
steps: أَنَا أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا عَادَةً،
لٰكِنَّ أَخِي يَسْتَيْقِظُ مُتَأَخِّرًا أَحْيَانًا.
نَحْنُ نُصَلِّي الفَجْرَ مَعًا دَائِمًا.
هُمْ (my cousins) يَدْرُسُونَ فِي مَدْرَسَةٍ قَرِيبَةٍ.
model.answer: Four persons, three frequency words

teach.note: Range of persons = higher marks.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Identity and culture - Daily life
lessons.title: Food, mealtimes and healthy eating
objectives: Talk about meals and eating habits
Give opinions about healthy and unhealthy food
Use comparisons and reasons in Arabic
starter: Say what you do in the morning and evening.
Say a sentence with 'sometimes' and a verb.
Name three foods in Arabic.

teach.heading: Meals
bullets: أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ - I eat breakfast at seven
نَتَنَاوَلُ الْغَدَاءَ مَعًا - we have lunch together
الْعَشَاءُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ مَسَاءً - dinner at 7pm
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Revise food vocabulary from Year 9. Ask pupils what they eat for each meal. The Prophet (peace be upon him) advised his companions to gather over their food and mention Allah's name so that there is blessing in it (Abu Dawud). The basic point is that eating together builds family bonds.

teach.heading: Healthy and unhealthy
bullets: الْخُضَارُ وَالْفَاكِهَةُ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلصِّحَّةِ - vegetables and fruit are good
الْوَجَبَاتُ السَّرِيعَةُ ضَارَّةٌ بِالصِّحَّةِ - fast food is bad
السُّكَّرِيَّاتُ - sukkariyyāt - sweets
الْمَاءُ مُهِمٌّ - water is important
teach.note: Plural things take a feminine singular adjective: الْوَجَبَاتُ السَّرِيعَةُ ضَارَّةٌ. Note ضَارٌّ with shadda. Ask pupils to classify foods into healthy and unhealthy. Include halal and tayyib: Qur'an 2:168 'eat of what is lawful and good'.

teach.heading: Moderation
bullets: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا - eat and drink and do not waste
أُحَاوِلُ أَنْ آكُلَ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا - I try to eat healthy food
لَا آكُلُ كَثِيرًا مِنَ السُّكَّرِيَّاتِ
teach.note: Qur'an 7:31: eat and drink but do not be extravagant. Link to health and not wasting food. Teach أُحَاوِلُ أَنْ + subjunctive. Pupils say one change they could make to be healthier.

teach.heading: Giving advice
bullets: يَجِبُ أَنْ نَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ - we must drink water
يَجِبُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ الْخُضَارَ - we must eat vegetables
لَا يَجِبُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْوَجَبَاتِ السَّرِيعَةِ
teach.note: Teach يَجِبُ أَنْ (it is necessary to) + verb with fatḥa. Practise giving advice to a friend. Also teach يُفَضَّلُ أَنْ (it is preferable to). Ask pupils to write three pieces of advice.

teach.heading: Speaking and writing
bullets: مَاذَا تَأْكُلُ عَادَةً؟ - what do you usually eat?
هَلْ تَأْكُلُ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا؟ - do you eat healthy food?
لِمَاذَا؟ - why?
teach.note: Practise three-question conversation. Model a full answer: 'I usually eat rice and chicken. I try to eat vegetables because they are good for health.' Pupils practise with a partner and swap.

practice: Say what you eat for breakfast and why.
Translate: 'Fast food is bad for health'.
Give advice using يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Say the Arabic for 'I try to eat healthy food'.
independent: Write a 80-word text on healthy eating with advice and reasons.
Make a survey of three people's food habits and report in Arabic.
Prepare a 1-minute talk 'Food in my life'.
exit: Write one sentence with يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Write one unhealthy food and one healthy food.
lessons.homework: Write a leaflet in Arabic (90 words) giving advice for a healthy diet, with at least four pieces of advice.
lessons.send: SEND: food cards with healthy/unhealthy labels. EAL: bilingual vocabulary with audio. Stretch: add comparisons, for example الْمَاءُ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ الْعَصِيرِ (water is better than juice).

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Identity and culture - Daily life
lessons.title: Technology and social media
objectives: Talk about technology and how we use it
Give advantages and disadvantages
Express and justify opinions about social media
starter: Give advice about healthy food using يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Say what you usually eat for lunch.
Translate: 'Water is important'.

teach.heading: What I use
bullets: أَسْتَعْمِلُ الْهَاتِفَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ - I use my phone every day
أَسْتَعْمِلُ الْحَاسُوبَ لِلدِّرَاسَةِ - I use the computer for study
أَلْعَبُ الْأَلْعَابَ الْإِلِكْتْرُونِيَّةَ - I play video games
أَتَوَاصَلُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي - I communicate with friends
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Introduce vocabulary and ask how pupils use technology. Remind them that use of phones for learning is a good use. Note the verb أَسْتَعْمِلُ (form X). The ل in لِلدِّرَاسَةِ means 'for'. Pupils give three uses.

teach.heading: Advantages
bullets: التِّكْنُولُوجْيَا تُسَهِّلُ الْحَيَاةَ - technology makes life easier
نَتَعَلَّمُ عَبْرَ الْإِنْتَرْنِتِ - we learn online
نَتَوَاصَلُ مَعَ الْعَائِلَةِ فِي الْخَارِجِ - with family abroad
teach.note: Elicit positive uses: learning, communication, saving time. Online school is itself an example. Use the connectors أَوَّلًا and ثَانِيًا (secondly). Pupils write three advantages.

teach.heading: Disadvantages
bullets: يُضَيِّعُ الْوَقْتَ - it wastes time
الْإِدْمَانُ عَلَى الْهَاتِفِ - addiction to the phone
قَدْ يَكُونُ خَطِيرًا - it may be dangerous
قِلَّةُ الْخُصُوصِيَّةِ - lack of privacy
teach.note: Discuss risks: wasting time, addiction, bullying, strangers and privacy. Connect to online safety taught in PSHE. Use the word قَدْ + present (may). Remind pupils of the hadith about two blessings many people lose: health and free time (Sahih al-Bukhari).

teach.heading: Giving a balanced opinion
bullets: مِنْ جِهَةٍ هُوَ مُفِيدٌ - on the one hand it is useful
وَمِنْ جِهَةٍ أُخْرَى هُوَ خَطِيرٌ - on the other hand it is dangerous
فِي رَأْيِي يَجِبُ أَنْ نَسْتَعْمِلَهُ بِحِكْمَةٍ - wisely
teach.note: Teach the pair مِنْ جِهَةٍ ... وَمِنْ جِهَةٍ أُخْرَى. Practise balanced answers. Pupils say 'in my opinion we must use it wisely'. Highlight بِحِكْمَةٍ (with wisdom).

teach.heading: Mini debate
bullets: هَلْ تَسْتَعْمِلُ وَسَائِلَ التَّوَاصُلِ؟
كَمْ سَاعَةً تَسْتَعْمِلُ الْهَاتِفَ؟ - how many hours?
هَلْ هُوَ مُفِيدٌ أَمْ ضَارٌّ؟ - useful or harmful?
teach.note: Pupils debate in pairs: one argues for, one against. Use opinion phrases. Collect points and write them on the board. Encourage respectful disagreement.

practice: Name three uses of a phone.
Give one advantage and one disadvantage of social media.
Translate: 'In my opinion we must use it wisely'.
Say how many hours you use your phone.
independent: Write a balanced paragraph of 90 words on social media.
Prepare a debate: 'Technology makes our life better'.
Record a 1-minute speaking answer.
exit: Write one advantage of technology.
Write one disadvantage and a piece of advice.
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word opinion article in Arabic: 'Technology and young people'.
lessons.send: SEND: advantages and disadvantages matching cards. EAL: bilingual vocabulary list. Stretch: add a conditional sentence with إِذَا.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Identity and culture - Daily life
lessons.title: Free time, sport and hobbies
objectives: Describe free-time activities and sport
Use the present, past and future tenses together
Explain why activities are important for health
starter: Give one advantage of technology in Arabic.
Say how often you use your phone.
Translate: 'My hobby is reading'.

teach.heading: Hobbies
bullets: هِوَايَتِي الْقِرَاءَةُ - hiwāyatī al-qirā'a - my hobby is reading
أُحِبُّ الرَّسْمَ - uḥibbu r-rasm - I like drawing
أُحِبُّ الطَّبْخَ - I like cooking
أَقْضِي وَقْتَ فَرَاغِي فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ - I spend my free time reading
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Build on Y7 hobbies. Introduce the verbal noun (masdar): الْقِرَاءَةُ, الرَّسْمُ, الطَّبْخُ. Use أَقْضِي وَقْتَ فَرَاغِي فِي + masdar as a chunk. Note the genitive after فِي. Pupils write their own hobby sentence.

teach.heading: Sport
bullets: أَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - I play football
أَسْبَحُ فِي الْمَسْبَحِ - I swim in the pool
أُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ - three times a week
كُرَةُ السَّلَّةِ - basketball
teach.note: Teach sports: كُرَةُ الْقَدَمِ, كُرَةُ السَّلَّةِ, السِّبَاحَةُ, الْجَرْيُ (running). The hadith: the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both (Sahih Muslim). Link to taking care of the body.

teach.heading: Past and future
bullets: أَمْسِ لَعِبْتُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - yesterday I played football
غَدًا سَأَسْبَحُ - tomorrow I will swim
فِي الْعُطْلَةِ سَنَلْعَبُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ - in the holiday we will play
teach.note: Combine tenses: present for habits, past for yesterday, future for plans. Pupils produce one sentence in each tense. Use a three-column table. Revise the past tense endings from Y8 and the future from Y9.

teach.heading: Why it matters
bullets: الرِّيَاضَةُ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلصِّحَّةِ - sport is good for health
تُقَوِّي الْجِسْمَ - it strengthens the body
تُخَفِّفُ التَّوَتُّرَ - it reduces stress
teach.note: Teach the benefits. Note that الرِّيَاضَةُ is feminine and so the adjective is feminine. Connect to mental health: PSHE topic. Pupils choose one benefit and explain it in a sentence.

teach.heading: Speaking task
bullets: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ فِي وَقْتِ فَرَاغِكَ؟
مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ فِي نِهَايَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي؟
مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ غَدًا؟
teach.note: Role-play with three tenses in questions. Pupils answer using the same tense as the question. Highlight how the question tells you which tense to use. Give feedback on accuracy.

practice: Say your hobby in Arabic.
Translate: 'I play football three times a week'.
Say what you did yesterday and what you will do tomorrow.
Give one benefit of sport.
independent: Write a 90-word text about your free time using all three tenses.
Interview a partner about their hobbies and write 5 sentences.
Prepare a 1-minute presentation.
exit: Write a sentence with أُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ.
Write a sentence in the future about sport.
lessons.homework: Write a short article for a school magazine (100 words) on 'Free time and health'.
lessons.send: SEND: hobby pictures with verbs. EAL: bilingual hobby list. Stretch: add a comparison between two sports.

lessons.title: Bridge: cultural life: Ramadan and Eid in three time frames
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I describe Ramadan and Eid using past, present and future?
objectives: To understand how to describe Ramadan and Eid using past, present and future verbs accurately
successCriteria: All: describe Ramadan in the present: نَصُومُ مِنَ الفَجْرِ إِلَى المَغْرِبِ
Most: say what I did last Eid and will do this Ramadan
Some: use three time frames and an opinion in one paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the lunar calendar and moon sighting
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the purpose of fasting is taqwa

hook.text: Ramadan starts in about three weeks. What will be the same as last year, and what do you want to do differently?
hook.a: Pupils' own; the goal of fasting is taqwa (al-Baqarah 2:183).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may attain taqwa' (al-Baqarah 2:183). Ramadan is the month in which the Qur'an was sent down (al-Baqarah 2:185).

starter.q: Bismillah. 'We study': A) نَدْرُسُ B) يَدْرُسُونَ
Name the two Eids in Arabic.

teach.heading: Ramadan now (present)
bullets: نَصُومُ مِنَ الفَجْرِ إِلَى المَغْرِبِ
نَتَسَحَّرُ قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ وَنُفْطِرُ عَلَى التَّمْرِ
نُصَلِّي التَّرَاوِيحَ وَنَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Hollow verb صَامَ / يَصُومُ: watch the long vowel.

teach.heading: Three time frames
teach.note: Hollow verbs shorten the long vowel in the past with ـتُ: صَامَ → صُمْتُ, زَارَ → زُرْتُ.

teach.heading: Eid
bullets: فِي العِيدِ نُصَلِّي صَلَاةَ العِيدِ وَنَلْبَسُ مَلَابِسَ جَدِيدَةً
نَزُورُ الأَقَارِبَ وَنَقُولُ: عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ
نُعْطِي زَكَاةَ الفِطْرِ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ
teach.note: Spec 1.3 festivals are taught through Ramadan and the two Eids.

teach.heading: Model: a three-tense paragraph

model.problem: صِفْ رَمَضَانَ وَالعِيدَ فِي أُسْرَتِكَ.
steps: Present: فِي رَمَضَانَ نَصُومُ وَنُفْطِرُ مَعًا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
Past: فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي زُرْنَا جَدَّتِي وَكَانَ يَوْمًا رَائِعًا.
Future: هٰذِهِ السَّنَةَ سَأَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ كُلَّهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.
Opinion: أُحِبُّ رَمَضَانَ لِأَنَّهُ شَهْرُ القُرْآنِ.
model.answer: Three time frames plus opinion

teach.note: This is a typical 1AA0 Paper 4 and 4AA1 Paper 2 topic.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Hollow verb: the long ا drops and the first vowel becomes u: صُمْتُ.

practice.q: Translate: Last Eid we visited my grandparents.
practice.a: فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي زُرْنَا جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي.
practice.model:
Time phrase: فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي.

Object: جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي.

What is سُحُور?

independent.a: Marked for three time frames (including hollow verbs), festival vocabulary, opinions with reasons and accuracy.
independent.model: Teacher writes the present-tense opening, then the past sentence.

independent.q: Extend (Group B): answer aloud: مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي؟ (unexpected question practice).
independent.a: Developed past-tense answer

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of رَائِعًا in كَانَ العِيدُ رَائِعًا.
independent.a: خَبَرُ كَانَ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ (predicate of kana, accusative, marked by fathah)
